title: Oka coherence and local coherent free resolutions

items.title: Coherent module sheaves on complex manifolds
items.statement:
Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space, so $X$ is a topological space and $\mathcal O_X$ is a sheaf of commutative rings. An $\mathcal O_X$-module sheaf $\mathcal F$ is **locally of finite type** if for every $x\in X$ there are an open neighborhood $U$ of $x$, a finite integer $r\ge0$, and sections $s_1,\ldots,s_r\in\mathcal F(U)$ such that their germs generate $\mathcal F_y$ as an $\mathcal O_{X,y}$-module for every $y\in U$.

For an open $V\subseteq X$, a finite integer $p\ge0$, and an $\mathcal O_X$-module morphism $\phi:\mathcal O_V^{\oplus p}\to\mathcal F|_V$, its **relation sheaf** is the kernel sheaf $\ker\phi$. The module sheaf $\mathcal F$ is **coherent** if it is locally of finite type and, for every such $V$, $p$, and $\phi$, the relation sheaf $\ker\phi$ is locally of finite type. Here $\mathcal O_V^{\oplus0}$ is the zero module sheaf.

In particular, for a finite tuple $f_1,\ldots,f_p\in\mathcal O_X(U)$, its holomorphic relation sheaf is the kernel of the morphism $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus p}\to\mathcal O_U$ that sends $(a_1,\ldots,a_p)$ to $\sum_{j=1}^p a_jf_j$. The structure sheaf is coherent when it is coherent as a module over itself. If $M$ is a complex manifold, an **analytic coherent module on $M$** means a coherent module sheaf over its sheaf $\mathcal O_M$ of holomorphic functions.
items.axiom_base: ZF; definition only, with no choice operation and no physical premise.

references.title: Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, Chapter II §3.3, Definition (3.18)

items.title: Finite free map kernels over a coherent structure sheaf are locally finite type
items.statement: Let $(X,\mathcal A)$ be a ringed space whose structure sheaf $\mathcal A$ is coherent in the sense that every finite tuple of its local sections has a locally finite-type relation sheaf. For all finite integers $p,q\ge0$ and every $\mathcal A$-module morphism $\Phi:\mathcal A^{\oplus p}\to\mathcal A^{\oplus q}$, the kernel sheaf $\ker\Phi$ is locally of finite type.
items.axiom_base: ZF; finite local algebraic constructions only, with no physical premise.

items.title: Local relations among Weierstrass polynomials reduce to bounded degree
items.statement: Let $n,q,d\ge1$ be integers, let $U'\subseteq\mathbb C^{n-1}$ and $D\subseteq\mathbb C$ be polydiscs, let $w$ denote the last coordinate, and let $P_1,\ldots,P_q\in\mathcal O(U')[w]$ be monic Weierstrass polynomials with $1\le\deg_w P_j\le d$. For every $x=(x',w_0)\in U'\times D$, each germ in the relation sheaf of $(P_1,\ldots,P_q)$ at $x$ is an $\mathcal O_{U'\times D,x}$-linear combination of relation germs whose components are polynomials in $w-w_0$ of degree at most $d$ with coefficients in $\mathcal O_{U',x'}$.
items.axiom_base: ZF; finite local algebraic constructions only, with no physical premise.

references.title: Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, Chapter II §3.3, Lemma 3.20
Joachim Wehler, Stein Manifolds, §4.2, Theorem 4.28 proof, Weierstrass reduction

items.title: Kernels, cokernels, and finite extensions of coherent module sheaves
items.statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space and use the coherence definition on the A page. The kernel and cokernel of any morphism between coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module sheaves are coherent. In every short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal F'\to\mathcal E\to\mathcal F''\to0$ of $\mathcal O_X$-module sheaves, if any two of $\mathcal F'$, $\mathcal E$, and $\mathcal F''$ are coherent, then the third is coherent.
items.axiom_base: ZF; finite local algebraic constructions only, with no physical premise.

items.title: Oka coherence and local coherent free resolutions
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional complex manifold and let $\mathcal O_M$ be its sheaf of holomorphic functions. For every open $U\subseteq M$ and every finite tuple $f_1,\ldots,f_q\in\mathcal O_M(U)$, the relation sheaf
$$
\ker\!\left(\mathcal O_U^{\oplus q}\longrightarrow\mathcal O_U,\quad(a_1,\ldots,a_q)\longmapsto\sum_{j=1}^q a_jf_j\right)
$$
is locally of finite type: every point has a neighborhood on which one finite family of relation sections generates the relation stalk at every point. Consequently $\mathcal O_M$ is coherent. Coherent $\mathcal O_M$-module sheaves are closed under kernels, cokernels, and finite extensions. For every coherent $\mathcal O_M$-module $\mathcal F$, point $x\in M$, and finite integer $\ell\ge0$, there are a chart neighborhood $W$ of $x$ and finite ranks $p_0,\ldots,p_\ell$ for which
$$
\mathcal O_W^{\oplus p_\ell}\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow\mathcal O_W^{\oplus p_0}\longrightarrow\mathcal F|_W\longrightarrow0
$$
is exact at $\mathcal F|_W$ and at every free term except the leftmost one. No exactness at the leftmost free term and no global analytic free resolution are asserted.
items.strategy: Prove the Weierstrass-induction relation lemma with generators uniform on one neighborhood, following Demailly II3.19–3.20. Handle zero/unit tuple entries and coordinate changes. Prove the elementary coherent-kernel calculus and obtain each finite partial resolution by successive coherent kernels and finite shrinking. Stalk Noetherianity alone is insufficient.
items.axiom_base: ZF + full AC as the approved ambient premise. The local proof uses only finite local selections and shrinkings; no arbitrary-index choice is claimed. No physical premise.

references.title: Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, Chapter II §3.3, Theorem 3.19 and Lemma 3.20

items.title: A holomorphic relation kernel on a bidisc
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice and let $D=D_1\times D_2\subset\mathbb C^2$ be a bidisc centered at the origin, with coordinate functions $z_1,z_2$. For the $\mathcal O_D$-linear map $\mu:\mathcal O_D^{\oplus2}\to\mathcal O_D$ given by $\mu(a,b)=z_1a+z_2b$, the relation sheaf is a coherent $\mathcal O_D$-module and is generated on $D$ by the section $(-z_2,z_1)$, including at the origin.
items.strategy: Prove divisibility and gluing, not just away-from-origin rank.

items.title: A coherent point quotient and its first syzygies
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $N\ge1$, let $D\subset\mathbb C^N$ be a polydisc centered at the origin with coordinates $z_1,\ldots,z_N$, and let $\mathcal F$ be the cokernel sheaf of $\mu:\mathcal O_D^{\oplus N}\to\mathcal O_D$, $\mu(a_1,\ldots,a_N)=\sum_{i=1}^N a_i z_i$. The stalk of $\mathcal F$ is $\mathbb C$ at the origin and zero at every other point of $D$. The sheaf $\mathcal F$ is coherent, and the kernel of $\mu$ is generated on $D$ by the coordinate Koszul sections $z_j e_i-z_i e_j$ for $1\le i<j\le N$; for $N=1$ this generating family is empty.
items.strategy: Use coordinate Koszul relations; do not assert global resolution from a stalk.
